I am 68 years old and have only been farming for one year, so I still have a lot to learn. I finished primary school a long time ago, and most of what I know comes from watching my neighbors here in Quzhou County. My household is just me and my wife — two mouths to feed, two pairs of hands to work with — so I cannot take on too much labor. I have 10.1 mu of land and a well for irrigation, which is good because the rain here on the North China Plain is never enough on its own.

Last year was my first year, and I saw that most families around me plant wheat in autumn and then maize right after the wheat harvest in June. That is the safest way — wheat and maize together give you two harvests in one year, and there is always a market for both. I also tried a small piece of cotton. Cotton brings decent money, but it is hard work for an old man — so much spraying! This year I will keep cotton on a smaller piece, 2.6 mu, and put the rest of my land, 7.5 mu, into the wheat-maize rotation like my neighbors.

For wheat, I will sow in October using improved seeds I buy from the township shop — about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing, I will do rotary tillage to prepare the ground. I will spread compound fertilizer as a basal dose and topdress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I will irrigate three times: once in the winter if the soil is too dry, and twice more in spring when the wheat is jointing and filling grain. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice, and if the spring is wet, I will add one fungicide spray to prevent rust.

For maize, after I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize — Denghai 605, like everyone else uses — directly into the wheat stubble without tilling. No-tillage saves time and fuel, and the neighbors say it works fine. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and maybe some extra nitrogen at the big trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice because my well can manage it, and I will spray for weeds once and insects twice.

For cotton, I will rotary till the 2.6 mu in April and sow improved Guoxinmian seeds. Cotton needs balanced fertilizer, so I will use compound fertilizer with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. I will irrigate twice during the summer drought. The hardest part is the insects — I will need to spray insecticide about 12 times, plus herbicide once and maybe a plant regulator, so that is about 14 sprays in total. At my age this is tiring, but 2.6 mu is manageable.

I expect about 1000 jin of wheat per mu, 1100 jin of maize per mu, and around 550 jin of cotton per mu — not the best in the village, but reasonable for someone with only one year of experience.
